newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai takes measures to build conglomerates.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai takes measures to build conglomerates.

text.p: The Shanghai city government has announced a series of measures to encourage the creation of major state-owned conglomerates in the city, the China Securities said on Monday.
The measures include giving the city's key state firms the power to independently make investment decisions, personnel changes and dispose of assets, the newspaper said.

"To promote the development of pillar industries and enhance economic efficiency, the Shanghai city government has recently promulgated a series of measures to support large-scale industrial groups," the newspaper said.

The pressure on state-owned firms to merge into larger groupings is one of the strategies being used by the government to help solve the problem of massive indebtedness and inefficiency in the state enterprise sector.
Groups which have surplus land will be allowed to sell it to developers and to include the income from the sales in their registered capital.
The groups will be given priority if they want to set up subsidiary firms to conduct foreign trade, the newspaper said.
If the groups take over other enterprises, they will enjoy any preferential policies enjoyed by the enterprises being taken over, it said.
